title: TrustFlow: Verifiable Agent Workflows
summary: TrustFlow turns natural-language tasks into inspectable synthetic workflows. Deterministic policy, hash-bound approvals, stable payment intents and ledger-grounded verification help prevent unauthorized or duplicate actions through timeouts and controlled crashes. The demo uses independently accepted fake-mode M5.2 evidence; live Meta Muse results remain pending.
full_description:
An agent can say a payment succeeded without establishing whether the exact action was authorized, whether it happened once, or what a timeout means. Retrying can be dangerous when a worker commits after its caller stops waiting.

TrustFlow explores this problem in a local financial sandbox with synthetic accounts and funds. A Planner proposes typed steps; a deterministic PolicyEngine decides risk. High-risk actions pause for a human decision bound to the plan version, payload and full SHA-256 hash. Approval freezes an isolated snapshot and authorizes its payment intents.

The Executor checks authorized payloads at the mutation boundary and uses stable operation identities as idempotency keys. SQLite atomically checks the key, changes balances and records the transaction. Verification independently reads ledger rows, matches authorized operations, checks intent coverage and confirms conservation. A semantic PASS cannot override deterministic failure.

The two-minute video uses actual Chromium screenshots from independently accepted M5.2, with clearly labelled editorial zooms rather than live footage. It shows exact-hash approval, a matching transaction, durable rejection, a late worker commit, missing mandatory evidence and recovery after SIGKILL at a real post-COMMIT checkpoint. Recovery verifies the original transaction without issuing another transfer. The accepted experiments cover four complete fake-mode replays; the separate 33-case offline regression evaluation is not a model benchmark.

The accepted source contains MetaResponsesProvider for structured planning and semantic review through Meta's Responses API, with flat strict schemas. Live Muse compatibility, quality, latency, usage and cost remain pending independently supported M5.3 evidence. The video uses FakeLLMProvider throughout.

After prerequisite installation, one command reproduces all six scenarios: python scripts/run_m52_demo.py --out artifacts/m5.2/latest. Manifests, screenshots and ledger observations make the outcome inspectable. This is a trusted local single-instance SQLite prototype with a shared demo token: no production banking readiness, public deployment, universal crash guarantee or container recreation durability is claimed.

meta_model_usage: The accepted source implements MetaResponsesProvider for schema-constrained planning and semantic review via POST /responses. Planning and review default to muse-wonder-1.0; muse-spark-1.3 is configured as a fast model. These are source configuration facts, not proof of live invocation. Accepted M5.2 and this video use FakeLLMProvider. Independently verified live M5.3 results: PENDING.
architecture: Next.js UI / FastAPI -> Planner -> deterministic PolicyEngine -> Human Approval when required -> Executor -> SQLite Ledger -> independent Verifier. A semantic reviewer uses the provider boundary after deterministic checks. Recovery reconciles existing operations and retries verification only. Audit payload hashes, workflow-scoped usage, evidence spans and manifests provide observability.
technical_novelty: The prototype connects an exact approved snapshot, backend-owned payment identity and independently read ledger evidence across timeout and post-COMMIT crash boundaries. Re-planning or recovery cannot silently turn a new step into permission for another transfer. This is an engineering design demonstrated in a controlled sandbox, not a new cryptographic primitive or universal distributed exactly-once guarantee.
reproducibility: Accepted runtime base: 38cc3942dbd715681d59bfd893e47643210294a9. The M5.4 branch preserves that implementation. Canonical command: python scripts/run_m52_demo.py --out artifacts/m5.2/latest. A fresh run records its own SHA and must independently pass; archived acceptance does not prove a new clean-machine run. Video export is local and uses existing presentation/evidence assets.
setup_instructions: Install Python 3.12+, Git, a running Linux-container Docker Engine and Compose 2.24.4+ with !override support. Create/activate a virtual environment, run python -m pip install -e ".[dev,demo]", then python -m playwright install chromium. From the repository root run python scripts/run_m52_demo.py --out artifacts/m5.2/latest. See README for platform notes, short Windows output paths and cleanup behavior. No model key is needed for fake mode.
limitations: Synthetic funds and tools; trusted local single instance; SQLite and a shared demo token; no production identity/RBAC or banking integration; no public deployment; controlled timeout and same-container SIGKILL checkpoints only; no universal crash/race or container recreation guarantee. Live Meta evaluation and independent M5.4 acceptance remain pending.
